newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey wants end to Iran diplomat row.
newsitem.headline: Turkey wants end to Iran diplomat row.

text.p: Turkey said on Monday it sought an end to a tit-for-tat diplomatic row with neighbour Iran that began with the presence of Tehran's ambassador at an Islamist protest in Ankara.
"We want to see that things return to normal based on mutual interest and the security concerns of both countries," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told reporters.
Turkish envoy Ali Tuygan arrived in Tehran on Saturday to deliver a message from President Suleyman Demirel to Iranian counterpart, Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
"We will communicate to them it is important that the two neighbouring countries should maintain mutually beneficial and fruitful relationship now and in the future," Atacanli said.
The row started when Ankara protested to Tehran early in February about comments by Iranian ambassador Mohammad Reza Bagheri at an Islamist rally in the Ankara district of Sincan.
Bagheri was accused as having praised sharia, the Islamic law. Urging a change to the secular system is forbidden in Turkey.

A Turkish military commander was quoted last week in the Turkish press as accusing Iran of "terrorism", sparking criticism from Iran's chief consul in the city of Erzurum who Ankara later declared persona non grata.
Iran said on Saturday it had ordered Turkey's ambassador and another Turkish diplomat in the western city of Orumiyeh to leave.

Diplomatic relations between the 18-year-old Islamic republic and its secularist neighbour have often been strained but the expulsions cap the first major row since an Islamist-led government came to power in Ankara last June.
